component.name: Apache Kudu
component.description: Distributed, columnar storage engine for fast analytics on fast-changing data. A cluster is a set of master servers (catalog/metadata, tablet placement) and tablet servers (row data in tablets, replicated via Raft consensus); clients talk to masters and tablet servers over RPC, an HTTP Web UI exposes status/metrics, and the master's embedded webserver can optionally serve a REST API for DDL. Kudu is designed to run inside a trusted cluster network; several security controls are optional and off by default.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it. The source is a v0 draft by the ASF Security team, not yet maintainer-ratified; most claims are marked inferred pending PMC confirmation.

blueprints.name: Kudu cluster deployment
blueprints.description: Long-running master and tablet-server daemons inside an organization's analytics cluster (often alongside Impala/Spark on a Kerberized network): clients cross the network boundary into master/tserver RPC, authenticated operations cross the authorization boundary (User/Superuser ACL, optional Ranger), peers replicate via Raft over inter-node RPC with internal X.509 certs/tokens, and tablet servers write to local storage (optionally encrypted via a KMS).

assets.name: Kudu master
assets.description: Catalog, metadata, tablet placement, and authz-token issuance over the master RPC port; optionally serves a REST API for DDL (--enable_rest_api, off by default) behind the same authn/authz gate as RPC DDL.

assets.name: Tablet servers
assets.description: Store and serve row data in Raft-replicated tablets; handle read/write/scan RPC from clients and inter-node replication traffic.

assets.name: Web UI
assets.description: HTTP(S) status port exposing status/metrics; row data is redacted by default but metadata/metrics are visible, and fine-grained (Ranger) authorization is not enforced on it.

assets.name: Local storage and WAL
assets.description: Data directories and write-ahead log on the local filesystem; unencrypted unless --encrypt_data_at_rest is enabled with a KMS.

zones.name: Cluster clients
zones.description: Impala, Spark, and Kudu API clients; untrusted until authenticated (Kerberos/token), but with the default rpc_authentication=optional, unauthenticated connections from reachable subnets are allowed.

zones.name: Kudu cluster daemons
zones.description: Masters and tablet servers on the trusted cluster network; peers authenticate via internal certs/tokens, and a compromised authenticated peer is the Byzantine-participant case.

zones.name: Operator infrastructure
zones.description: Kerberos KDC, Ranger, KMS, daemon flags, keytabs, and hosts: provisioned and trusted by the operator; out of Kudu's model.

assumptions.description: Kudu assumes a trusted cluster network; with authentication optional, the cluster does not prevent access from unauthenticated users, so network-level controls are load-bearing until the operator sets rpc_authentication=required.
Kerberos, Ranger, and the KMS are provisioned and trusted by the operator when those features are enabled.
Daemons open RPC and HTTP listening sockets, read/write local data dirs and the WAL, talk to KDC/Ranger/KMS, and are not expected to run as root.

threats.name: Unauthenticated access under the default rpc_authentication=optional
threats.description: The default --rpc_authentication=optional allows unauthenticated connections from reachable subnets; the docs tell operators to set =required to secure a cluster. An unauthenticated-accessible cluster reachable by attackers is treated as an operator posture choice, not a Kudu defect (pending the PMC's explicit insecure-default ruling). 'Optional' does not mean 'authentication on': it authenticates if offered and otherwise allows.

threats.name: Authentication bypass on a required-auth cluster
threats.description: An unauthenticated client performs an RPC that requires identity on a cluster configured with rpc_authentication=required (Kerberos / internal tokens). Critical severity.

threats.name: Authenticated principal exceeds its ACL or Ranger grant
threats.description: A legitimate principal reads/writes a table or column its coarse User/Superuser ACL or fine-grained Ranger policy forbids, escalates via authz-token handling, or reaches admin RPCs reserved for the Superuser ACL. Critical severity. Note the User ACL default of '*' grants user-level access to all authenticated principals, not 'no access'.

threats.name: Plaintext RPC under the default rpc_encryption=optional
threats.description: With the default --rpc_encryption=optional, RPC may be plaintext and wire confidentiality/integrity is not guaranteed; plaintext RPC under the default is operator responsibility, and in-transit protection is a claimed property only when =required. Loopback (same-host) connections are not TLS-protected by design even then, unless --rpc_encrypt_loopback_connections is set.

threats.name: Row data exposed in the Web UI despite redaction
threats.description: The Web UI redacts row data by default while exposing schema, metrics, and cluster state by design; row values appearing in the Web UI would violate the redaction property (high severity). Metadata exposure itself is by design, and fine-grained authorization is not enforced on the Web UI.

threats.name: No fine-grained authorization on the Web UI
threats.description: Ranger policies are not enforced on the Web UI, which is gated only by its own coarse controls; treating the Web UI as a fine-grained-authz surface is a mistake. Disclaimed by the model.

threats.name: Unencrypted data files on disk by default
threats.description: Data files are plaintext on disk unless --encrypt_data_at_rest is enabled together with a KMS; a documented default, so readable data files given disk access are operator responsibility rather than a defect.

threats.name: Compromised authenticated peer in Raft replication
threats.description: A compromised tablet or master server that passed the internal X.509 cert/token handshake and then behaves arbitrarily. Raft replication safety (a committed write is durable and consistent across replicas) is claimed given fewer than a majority of faulty replicas; divergent replicas, a lost commit, or split-brain within that bound is critical. Compromise of a majority or more of replicas is out of scope.

threats.name: Denial of service against RPC/HTTP surfaces
threats.description: Volumetric or resource-exhaustion attacks against the RPC/HTTP surfaces are out of scope for this v0 model; availability is not a committed property. Whether an authenticated client triggering super-linear CPU/memory via crafted scans is in-model (versus a by-design expensive query) is an open maintainer question; the proposal is that only pre-authentication exhaustion would be in-model.

threats.name: Compromise of the operator or surrounding infrastructure
threats.description: The operator/admin and anyone with the daemon flags or keytabs has already won; the Kerberos KDC, Ranger service, KMS, HDFS, OS, and cluster network fabric are integrated with but not owned by Kudu. Out of scope.

trustBoundaries.name: Client RPC and HTTP trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The primary trust boundary is the authentication plus authorization layer (Kerberos/token auth, then coarse ACL, then optional Ranger fine-grained policy) when the operator has enabled enforcement; with auth optional (the default), unauthenticated connections from reachable subnets are allowed and network placement is load-bearing.

trustBoundaries.name: Operator infrastructure boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Daemon flags, ACLs, Kerberos/Ranger/KMS configuration, keytabs, and hosts are trusted operator inputs; anything requiring their control is out of model.

controls.name: Set --rpc_authentication=required
controls.description: Enforce Kerberos / internal-token client authentication (or keep the cluster strictly on a trusted, isolated network); the default 'optional' authenticates if offered and otherwise allows.

controls.name: Set --rpc_encryption=required
controls.description: Enable TLS wire confidentiality/integrity for RPC; add --rpc_encrypt_loopback_connections if same-host RPC must also be encrypted, since loopback connections are not TLS-protected by default (a performance-motivated design choice).

controls.name: Narrow the User and Superuser ACLs
controls.description: Move the User ACL away from the '*' default (which grants user-level access to all authenticated principals) to the intended principals, and reserve the Superuser ACL for admins.

controls.name: Enable Apache Ranger fine-grained authorization
controls.description: Wire the optional Ranger integration (Kudu 1.12+) for table/column-level policy in multi-tenant clusters; note it is not enforced on the Web UI.

controls.name: Enable --encrypt_data_at_rest with a KMS
controls.description: Enable at-rest encryption plus a KMS where disk confidentiality matters; data files are otherwise plaintext on disk.

controls.name: Web UI row-data redaction
controls.description: The Web UI redacts row data by default while exposing schema, metrics, and cluster state; keep redaction on.

controls.name: Front or restrict the Web UI
controls.description: Put the Web UI (and the optional REST API) behind an authenticating proxy or restrict its network exposure; fine-grained authorization is not enforced there.

controls.name: Internal certificate/token authentication on inter-node channels
controls.description: Masters and tablet servers authenticate peers via internal X.509 certs/tokens on inter-node RPC and Raft channels (pending maintainer confirmation of the exact boundary).

controls.name: Raft consensus replication
controls.description: Committed writes are durable and consistent across tablet replicas given fewer than a majority of faulty replicas; Raft tolerates a minority of faulty replicas.

controls.name: Protect keytabs, flagfiles, and data directories
controls.description: Restrict host filesystem permissions on keytabs, flagfiles, and data dirs; do not run daemons as root.
